dedupe_keys.name: evacuation experiment in shanghai tower stairwell walking speed from the 126th floor

description: A preprint reporting a full-scale evacuation experiment in Shanghai Tower, at 583 m the second tallest building in the world, by researchers from Shanghai universities and the Shanghai Research Institute of Building Science. Ninety participants aged 20 to 51 walked downstairs at their preferred speed through a stairwell with about 1.2 m wide stairs, 0.155 m risers and 0.25 m treads, starting from three floors: 44 from the 126th floor, 30 from the 117th and 16 security guards from the 100th. Movement was extracted from surveillance cameras on stair landings, in a bright morning without rain. Lessons: pedestrians choose a suitable velocity that falls with the target height, the group starting 9.63 percent higher took 16.39 percent longer, and speed within a group did not fall with distance. Coverage: one stairwell. Access: free preprint; the article gives no data file; the paper is CC BY-SA 4.0. Caveats: results are from one experiment with volunteers. It informs stairwell evacuation models, refuge floor planning and emergency response for very tall buildings; related records are not yet linked.
